    Skills & stack

    What I bring to a project.

    User interface design

    Clear hierarchy, considered type and colour, components that feel crafted.

    User experience design

    Flows built around what people are trying to do, with fewer steps and less guessing.

    Responsive web design

    Layouts that adapt from phone to wide desktop without breaking.

    Design systems

    Tokens and reusable components so every page feels related.

    Prototyping & wireframing

    From rough boxes to clickable flows before code is written.

    Front-end development

    Semantic HTML, modern CSS and modular JavaScript.

    Back-end development

    APIs with validation, error handling and security headers.

    API integration

    One API client, live and offline modes, honest error states.

    Database design

    Data shapes that keep business rules simple and safe.

    Performance

    Zero dependencies, lazy rendering, animations that pause off-screen.

    Accessibility

    Keyboard support, contrast checks, reduced-motion support, alt text.

    Version control & deployment

    Git workflows, CI tests and automated GitHub Pages deploys.

    Process

    Six steps, no surprises.

    1. 01

      Discover

      Understand the goal, the audience and the constraints. Ask "what does success look like?"

    2. 02

      Define

      Turn findings into user flows, content structure and a clear scope.

    3. 03

      Design

      Wireframes first, then a visual system: type, colour, components, motion.

    4. 04

      Build

      Semantic, modular front end and a validated back end that never trusts the client.

    5. 05

      Test

      Automated tests, keyboard and screen-reader checks, real devices, slow connections.

    6. 06

      Launch

      Deploy, measure, and keep improving based on real feedback.

    About me

    Curious by nature. Precise by habit.

    I'm Liorgio Ilanan, a web designer and developer from North Caloocan, Philippines. I love turning ideas into useful, thoughtful websites: first by understanding who they're for, then by designing and building every layer myself.

    This portfolio is my studio. Every project started as a small exercise and was rebuilt with a real back end, tests and a proper design system as I learned more. I learn by building, and I'm always building something.

    FAQ

    Good questions.

    Are these real client projects?

    No. Each project is labelled. "Live Demo" projects are built and working in this portfolio. "Concept Project" and "UI/UX Exploration" items are self-initiated design studies that show how I think. None are presented as client work.

    What can you help with?

    Interface and UX design for websites and apps, responsive front-end development, and small full-stack builds such as ordering flows, dashboards and APIs.

    Can I see the code?

    Yes. The whole portfolio, including the Node.js API and the tests, is in my GitHub repository.

    How do you approach a new project?

    Discover, define, design, build, test, launch. The process section above explains each step.
